instructions.instruction: Table names are prefixed with "Thc" to ensure they are unique in the database. This is transparent to the user, so they will refer to the tables without the prefix (e.g., "Appointment" instead of "ThcAppointment" or "BlogComment" instead of "ThcBlogComment"). AI must use the prefixed table names when interacting with the database such as requesting schema XML or executing SQL statements. Each table node in this XML section contains a `publicName` attribute containing the name of the table from the user's perspective (the non-prefixed name). AI should use this `publicName` attribute to locate the table(s) that are applicable to the user's request and when returning content to the user. This ensures this prefixing behavior remains transparent to the user.

table.name: ThcOntraportListFieldOption
table.description: Ontraport has a concept of a "list" data type that can be assigned to a field. The "list" data type is essentially a multi-select Enum, which means that a field can contain multiple selections out of a predefined set of options. This is in contrast to an Enum field that can only reference 1 predefined value at a time. Ontraport saves the selected options to these "list" fields as a string in the format: `/<optionId>/<optionId>/`. This makes it impossible to search efficiently, and also makes it impossible to perform complex queries like searching for records that have optionA OR optionB. The solution is to compile all options across all "list" fields within an Ontraport account into this centralized model. The primary key of this model is the ID of each option, which is possible because the ID that Ontraport assigns to each predefined "list" field option is unique for the entire account instead of just the field. Then, to make these options searchable for each record, a separate model is created for each "list" field to contain many-to-many associations between the records on the original model and the record's selected options (e.g., the values in the textual representation of the options). In short, the textual representation is inflated into records to form a proper association at the database level. These "field" models have 2 foreign fields: `optionId` which references the ID on this model, and a `recordId` field that references the ID on the original model. Altogether, this makes it possible to perform complex searches for records based on their chosen options. Furthermore, since this model contains the friendly name for each option ID, searches can also be performed based on the options's name instead of its numeric ID. This is crucial because users are only familiar with the option name, not its numeric ID. While this model can be searched directly, it is primary use-case is to join a field model to this model using its `optionId` foreign field in order to reference the name of an option.

column.name: id
column.description: The ID of the predefined option for the list field.

column.name: description
column.description: The description of the option, if available.

column.name: fieldId
column.description: The Ontraport ID of the field on the model that defines this option. As with the `objectId` field on this model, this is primarily for searching this model directly. When searching for the options associated with a particular record, use the field model that contains the many-to-many associations between records on the original model and their chosen options since the field models have an `optionId` foreign field referencing the id of the record on this model that represents the option.

column.name: name
column.description: The name of the option. This is useful because users aren't familiar with the numeric ID of each option. Typically, searches will involve the field model that contains many-to-many associations between records on the original model and their chosen options. Then, the field model can be joined to this model using its `optionId` foreign field to then reference the option's name.

table.name: ThcContactPatientFocusOption
table.description: A many-to-many association between the ThcContact model's records and the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model. The associations are derived from the ThcContact model's patient_focus_options_as_text field, which contains a textual representation of all selected options as a concatenated string with custom separators. However, the textual representation makes it impossible to perform efficient searches. As a result, the patient_focus_options_as_text field's value is inflated into records on this model to build a proper many-to-many association at the database level. See the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model for full details, as that model is necessary to derive the name of the options referenced by the `optionId` foreign field on this model. Note that for this relationship, the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model's `objectId` field = "0" and its `fieldId` field = "f2597". This is useful when searching the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model directly for options applicable to the ThcContact model's patient_focus_options_as_text field, although typically you will use this model (ThcContactPatientFocusOption) when querying for options since it contains the `recordId` property to understand what options a record is associated with.

column.name: id
column.description: The ID of the ThcContactPatientFocusOption. This is generated automatically by combining the `optionId` and `recordId` values.

column.name: optionId
column.description: The optionId assigned by Ontraport. This references the `id` on the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model, making it possible to join this model to the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model to reference the name of the option. Users are only familiar with the option name, not its numeric ID. This ID represents a single entry in the ThcContact model's patient_focus_options_as_text field (the text field with a serialized representation of all options associated with the record).

column.description: The ID of the ThcContact record that the option is associated with.

table.name: ThcItemConditionsOption
table.description: A many-to-many association between the ThcItem model's records and the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model. The associations are derived from the ThcItem model's conditions_options_as_text field, which contains a textual representation of all selected options as a concatenated string with custom separators. However, the textual representation makes it impossible to perform efficient searches. As a result, the conditions_options_as_text field's value is inflated into records on this model to build a proper many-to-many association at the database level. See the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model for full details, as that model is necessary to derive the name of the options referenced by the `optionId` foreign field on this model. Note that for this relationship, the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model's `objectId` field = "10003" and its `fieldId` field = "f2760". This is useful when searching the ThcOntraportListFieldOption model directly for options applicable to the ThcItem model's conditions_options_as_text field, although typically you will use this model (ThcItemConditionsOption) when querying for options since it contains the `recordId` property to understand what options a record is associated with.

column.name: id
column.description: The ID of the ThcItemConditionsOption. This is generated automatically by combining the `optionId` and `recordId` values.
